title: Billie Holiday as a young singer
summary: He met her in 1929, urged her not to drink wine, and blames her stepmother for her troubles.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: What about people like Lester Young and Billie Holiday?
Billie was a sweetheart.
What was your impression of Billie Holiday?
I loved her. I started to help her start all over.
How did you help her?
got to the Loew's got to the place, she got on stage there, she got to sing

She would do more for me than she would for her father. She went right in 129th Street where we used to hang out, after hours, and she was drinking wine. You know, we'd sit back and the musicians play and sang... So I used to tell her - I talked to her all the time and I'd say, 'Billie, now don't drink too much wine because you've got to sing.....' She made me a promise that she wouldn't do it, and she didn't. She was just a good kid. Her stepmother was the cause of all of it.
Her stepmother? Did you meet her?
I sure did.
What was the first time you met Billie Holiday?
I met Billie Holiday when I first came to New York in 1929.
How old was she then?
Oh, I don't know. She was old enough to know right from wrong. I guess she was about 16 or 17, something like that.
Did she have a big reputation at that time?
No, not at that time.
She was just singing around New York?
Yeah.
She had just come here or something?
Yeah. A nice kid, very nice, all the time.
But she was drinking when you first met her?
Mm-hm, she was drinking wine, sometimes top and
bottom; she'd mix it like that, you know.
Was she into anything else, prostitution or any other -
Not that I know of. Never heard of it.
